decisions.reason: The allowed real-valued real coordinate polynomial Re(z) has P_1(i)=0 but iP_1(1)=i; complex multilinearity was not defined for that target. The repaired definition specifies complex-coordinate polynomials with complex target, and retains real-coordinate polynomials on the underlying real Lie algebra. Coefficient extraction gives the unique polarization over the specified scalar field, and differentiating simultaneous conjugation invariance gives the stated bracket identity. Determinant coefficients and the real Pfaffian remain included.

At n=4 the fiber has basis 1,x,x^2,e(Q); the old three-class list does not meet the Leray–Hirsch hypothesis. Step 1.11 now supplies all Euler powers through n−2 and the even-rank complementary Euler class, then pulls this full family to the CW model. The relative CP/RP calculation gives the stated dimensions; xe(Q)=0 and e(Q)^2=(-1)^(n/2−1)x^(n−2) prove middle-degree independence. Fibration comparison transfers injectivity and the finite tower preserves properness. Also removed the false claim that Gr_2^+(R^2) is a point: rank two uses no Grassmann stage. The Statement is unchanged.

F6 mislabeled the rank in its real-bundle supplier: C is real two-dimensional. Corrected F6 to real rank two. Step 1.1 already supplies multiplication by i and the standard Hermitian metric, making the complex rank one explicit. The imaginary scalar forms give Hermitian connections, curvature i dx wedge dy, and c1 difference d(-x dy/(2pi)); the witness and its unchanged Statement are valid. This is a nonfatal citation-restatement defect because the missing complex structure was already supplied in the proof.

CP^0 is a point with H_2=H^2=0, so F6 overstates the two-cell argument. Restricted its H_2 and restriction-isomorphism assertions to m>=1 and stated the zero case separately. Proof 1.3 already made precisely this split, so the defect is nonfatal. The tautological period and projected-section local index are both −1; finite dual frames near each compact smooth cycle reduce the general base to finite projective space, and real UCT detects equality. Transgression gives the arbitrary complex-connection clause without changing the Statement.

The proposed counterexample changes the kind of orientation supplied. The geometric orientation definition def-oriented-real-vector-bundle-and-oriented-frame-bundle (used by the real splitting supplier F4) explicitly gives a rank-zero bundle only its canonical orientation. F10 also explicitly requires the standard unit orientation at rank zero. The broader R-oriented Thom definition in F11 allows o=−1, but the geometric zero-bundle orientation here induces o=1; hence e(0)=1 agrees with the empty Pfaffian. Positive-rank comparison follows from line normalization, block determinant/Pfaffian products, and injective flag pullback. Arbitrary-real-connection Pontryagin comparison uses real GL-invariant polynomials and connection independence. No edit is warranted.

The zero bundle over a point is flat but its canonical Thom Euler class is 1 in H^0, disproving old clause 3. The repaired clause keeps this case with its exact unit value and restricts Euler vanishing to rank 2m>0, where the degree-m Pfaffian at zero curvature vanishes. Step 4.1 now proves that clause explicitly. Positive Chern and Pontryagin forms vanish at zero curvature; real parts of complex transgression primitives justify comparison to a Hermitian connection. For the nonmetric witness, the genus-two tangent circle Euler number is −2; its mod-two Thom lift yields a fiberwise double cover with Euler number −1 and lifted SL(2,R) discrete transitions, whose zero local connection matrices glue.
